newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan releases two opposition members.
newsitem.headline: Sudan releases two opposition members.

text.p: Sudan has released two of the four leading southern opposition politicians it arrested earlier this week, southern Sudanese sources said on Friday.
They said the two politicians, former government minister Joseph Ukel and former regional minister Izaya Mabior, were questioned about their connections with Abel Alier, a former vice president.

The two were arrested along with former parliamentarian Joshua Dau on Tuesday in Khartoum. Security forces also picked up on Monday Ezeikel Kodi, a businessman and a former regional minister in southern Sudan, as he left Alier's law offices.
Sudan arrested the politicians just days after it rounded up dozens of opponents suspected of planning assassinations and sabotage acts in Khartoum, the sources had said on Thursday.
All four are vociferous critics of the Islamist government of Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir and they have often complained that the state is not giving southern Sudanese their rights.

Alier said in a recent letter to Bashir and influential Islamist leader Hassan al-Turabi that establishment of an Islamic state in Sudan has made non-Moslems and non-Arabs foreigners in their own land.
He also accused the government of detaining hundreds of politicians, labour leaders, students and professionals without due process of the law and holding them in unknown places.
Rebels in the mostly Christian and animist south have been fighting for autonomy from the Khartoum government since 1983.

They joined northern opposition members last month to wage an armed offensive in the south and east which the rebels say is aimed at pressuring the state and sparking a popular uprising -- the way previous governments in Sudan have fallen.
